input.brief: Offshore talent firm: vetted India-based professionals working U.S. hours (VA, RPO, accounting, legal, web dev), HQ Wilmington DE

direction.name: Type and nothing else
direction.idea: The first screen is made only of words, colour and space, good enough that nobody misses a picture there. Pictures arrive later, large and few, as relief from the type. This is the honest answer when a subject has nothing worth photographing: instead of inventing illustrations, set what you have to say as well as it can be set. The typography carries a point of view through scale (one enormous statement, everything else small), through measure (a narrow, bookish column or a full-width line), and through one committed colour.
direction.composition: First screen: the statement, two lines at most, set at 9–14vw and occupying the full width with tight leading, positioned in the upper two-thirds. One supporting sentence at 20–24px sits bottom-left on the same margin and the single action sits bottom-right on the same baseline. No navigation bar; two or three links in a top corner. Sections that follow are typographic set pieces, each different: a list of five to eight capabilities set at 4–6vw one per line; a paragraph at 28–36px in a 28ch column pushed to the right half; a pair of large numerals with a sentence each; a single quotation filling a colour field. Each section uses a different horizontal position (left, right, full) so the page has movement without imagery.
direction.typography: This direction lives or dies on the face and its settings. Display at tight tracking and leading; text sizes few and far apart (for example 15, 22, 34 and the display size). Use real typographic detail: proper quotes, balanced line breaks, hung punctuation where it helps.
direction.colour: Either one saturated ground for the whole page with a single ink, or paper and ink with one section inverted and one in the accent as a full field. Colour does the job images would have done.
direction.imagery: The first screen has no picture. Further down, real pictures of the subject's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs) arrive large and few: a full-bleed photograph between two type sections, a looping clip in one band, an archival image beside a list. Do not add icons, shapes, patterns or abstract graphics to compensate for anything.
direction.richness: Scale contrast and colour mass. A capability list set at 5vw is an image in its own right.
direction.pitfalls: Without pictures, weak copy has nowhere to hide: write real sentences. Vary the set pieces; four sections of big-heading-plus-paragraph is a text document, not a design. Keep all headings within two lines.

hero.name: Two-line statement, full width
hero.blueprint: Paper and ink only; no image. The wordmark at 15px sits top-left and two or three text links at the same size top-right, both on 24px margins; there is no bar. The statement fills the upper two thirds: two lines at clamp(96px, 12.5vw, 200px), medium to bold weight, tracking -0.05em, leading 0.86, starting 15% below the top edge. The first line is flush to the left margin and the second flush to the right margin, so the pair spans the full width and steps across the screen. Size the type so the longer line runs margin to margin: tune the vw value to the character count and test it at 1440 and 390. Between the statement and the bottom row about 18% of the height is left empty. The bottom row sits on one baseline 28px above the bottom edge: one supporting sentence at 22px on the left, max 44ch on two lines, and the single action bottom-right as a solid ink rectangle with square corners. There is no colour beyond ground and ink.
hero.mobile: Both lines turn flush left on 16px margins at 17vw, leading 0.9, starting at 14% of the height and filling the width. A gap of about 20% of the screen follows. The sentence sits at 17px above a full-width action, both anchored to the bottom with 20px to spare. Navigation reduces to the wordmark and one menu word.
hero.headline: A 3-5 word statement on two lines, at most 11 characters per line so 17vw type fits a phone.

palette.name: Sand and moss
palette.note: Sand grey holds the page with charcoal type, and one deep leaf-green band may close it. Moss green is reserved for buttons; brighter greens and blues arrive only through photographs.

photos.note: hands at work, craft and making

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Edge-to-edge heavy paragraph
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed flat colour field, at least 90svh tall, filled by one paragraph and nothing else. The paragraph is 35–55 words in the heaviest weight at clamp(36px, 5vw, 76px), leading 0.98, left-aligned, running from a 16px left margin to a 16px right margin so its lines reach both edges; use `text-wrap: pretty` and no hyphenation. No heading: the paragraph is the section. In two or three places a word-sized gap (an inline-block spacer 2.5em wide) opens inside a line. One small photograph, 9vw wide at 4:5 with square corners, is absolutely placed over the first two lines, rotated 4 degrees, covering parts of two words; a second chip at 6vw may sit in one of the gaps. Text takes the field's assigned ink at full contrast. The field butts against the section above with no space between them. On a page without images, drop the chips and close the gaps.
sections.mobile: The same field and weight at 9.5vw with leading 1.0 and 14px margins, so each line holds two or three words and the paragraph runs about fourteen lines. Remove the inline gaps. The photograph chip grows to 26vw and sits over the right end of lines three and four, still tilted.

sections.name: Statement cell, dark rows
sections.blueprint: Two halves butted together, each 50vw wide and at least 90svh tall, with no gap. Left half, in a pale tone: the heading in three short lines at clamp(36px, 4.2vw, 68px), its middle line pushed flush right while the first and third stay flush left (text-align set per line), so the block zigzags inside the cell. A two-sentence paragraph of 30ch sits at the bottom-left and the single action at the bottom-right on the same baseline. Right half, in the darkest tone: four or five rows of equal height filling it, told apart by alternating two near-black tones, not by lines. Each row is a three-part grid: a title at 28px (5 parts), a short paragraph at 16px (4 parts) and a plain list of three terms at 15px (3 parts), all top-aligned with 28px padding. No images anywhere in the section.
sections.mobile: The halves stack. The light cell comes first at 70svh with the zigzag heading at 10vw and the paragraph at its foot. The dark rows follow at full width; each row stacks its title and paragraph, and its three terms run inline as one sentence separated by commas. Rows keep the alternating tones.

sections.name: Figures inside a sentence
sections.blueprint: The numbers are written into prose and the prose is set at display size. One paragraph of two or three sentences, 22–34 words, containing three or four true figures, in the pattern 'Since 2014 we have rebuilt 340 roofs in 9 towns, and 312 of them have never leaked.' Set at clamp(32px, 4.4vw, 72px), leading 1.12, in columns 2–11, left-aligned and vertically centred in a section of 80–90svh with nothing else in it. Words are in the soft ink at regular weight; the figures alone are in full ink (or the accent) at the same size, in lining numerals, with non-breaking spaces binding each figure to its unit. No boxes, underlines or colour chips behind the figures. A visually hidden two-word heading names the section for structure; to the eye the paragraph stands alone. On a deep ground use a light weight and a soft light ink, with the figures in the brightest ink.
sections.mobile: The paragraph is 7.4vw with leading 1.2, at full width between 20px margins, vertically centred in 70svh. Keep each figure and its unit together on one line with non-breaking spaces. Nothing else appears in the section.

sections.name: Quiet ledger, side preview
sections.blueprint: A plain ledger in one column 560px wide whose left edge sits at 22% of the viewport width. A heading of two or three words at 24–28px in medium weight, then 32px of space, then one row per project, 44px tall: the name at 16px in full ink at the left, the kind of work at 14px in the soft ink starting at 55% of the column, and the year right-aligned with tabular figures. Nothing is drawn between rows; the three fixed starts make the columns. Hovering or focusing a row keeps it in full ink, drops the others to the soft ink, and shows that project's image in the empty area right of the column: a 4:3 frame 300px wide, `position: absolute`, its top aligned to the hovered row, 64px from the column's right edge, appearing with a 150ms fade. Holds 6–20 rows; group by year with 28px of extra space.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Rows are 52px tall: name at the left, year at the right, kind of work on a second line at 13px. There is no hover preview; instead the first three projects each show a 16:10 image at full column width above their row.

sections.name: Lines that step across
sections.blueprint: The sequence is written, not counted. Four lines of display type, one stage per line, each a complete short clause that begins with its order word: 'First you send it.' 'Then we take it apart.' 'You choose one.' 'It ships on Friday.' Set at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 76px), leading 1.0, one line each. The first line starts on column 1 and each following line starts two columns further right (grid-column-start 1, 3, 5, 7), so the block descends as a staircase and the eye follows the diagonal. Under each line, on that line's own left edge and 12px below, a sentence of up to 34ch at 17px in the soft ink. 56px between stages. The last line may take the accent colour as the single emphasis. The first line serves as the heading; there is no title above. Leave the columns to the left of the final stage empty.
sections.mobile: Lines drop to 8.4vw and may wrap onto a second line. The staircase becomes a smaller indent of 6vw per stage, so the fourth line starts 18vw in. Each sentence sits under its line at 16px on the same indent. 40px between stages.

sections.name: One long letter
sections.blueprint: A single testimonial given room to be read, set like a letter. One column 34–38ch wide begins at column 5 of 12, or shares the page's own reading column. The first sentence of the quotation is pulled up as the opening line at 28–32px in medium weight, two lines at most. The rest follows as two or three ordinary paragraphs at 18–19px with leading 1.55 and 20px between paragraphs, in the full ink, not grey. It closes the way a letter does: 40px of space, then the name on one line and the role on the next at 16px. In columns 1–3, top-aligned with the first line, sits either nothing or one small square photograph of the writer, 120px wide. There are no quotation marks at all; the letter form makes them unnecessary. Space above and below is 140px.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 20px margins. If there is a photograph it goes first at 96px square, left-aligned. Opening sentence at 24px, body at 17px, sign-off beneath. Nothing else changes; this section is already a phone composition.

sections.name: Side facts, wide paragraph
sections.blueprint: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width. Row one: in a 160px column at the left margin, three label and value pairs stack with 20px between them, each a label in the soft ink with its value beneath in full ink, all at 13px (founded, based in, team size). From the 34% line a five-line paragraph at clamp(20px, 1.7vw, 26px), leading 1.35, runs to 90% of the width. Row two starts 120px lower and repeats the logic for the record of the practice: one plain word at 13px at the far left (awards, press, clients), then from the 34% line two list columns, each 260px wide with a 64px gutter, at 13px with 10px between lines: name at the left, year at the right in the soft ink. No heading; the paragraph opens the section. Each list comfortably holds 6–12 lines. No photographs are needed.
sections.mobile: Everything aligns to the left margin. The paragraph comes first at 19px. The three label and value pairs follow as a two-column grid at 14px. The two record lists stack with 40px between them, each opened by its plain word in full ink.

sections.name: One item per poster line
sections.blueprint: A short list set as a poster. Four to seven items (services, headline acts, courses, opening days) stack one per line at clamp(64px, 10vw, 150px) in the display weight, all capitals or all lowercase, leading 0.92, flush left at a 20px margin on a flat field. Its one detail (a price, a date, a time range) sits at the right margin on the same baseline at 18–20px with tabular figures, so the page has two alignments only: giant words left, small facts right. Items too long for one line at this size are shortened, not shrunk. Between items there is only the tight leading. Hovering an item swaps its ink for the accent. There is no heading: the first item starts 80px below the section top and the last ends 80px above the bottom. The list reuses the hero title's exact type size, so it reads as another poster.
sections.mobile: Items at 15vw, one per line, flush left with 16px margins. Each detail moves beneath its item at 15px, left-aligned, with 6px above and 22px below. If any single word is wider than the screen at 15vw, drop the whole list to 12vw rather than breaking a word.

sections.name: One word is the button
sections.blueprint: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
sections.mobile: The band is 46svh tall. The word is set at whatever size fills the width on one line; choose a shorter verb rather than going below 22vw. Sentence top-left at 17px across two lines, arrow top-right at 32px. The whole band stays tappable.

sections.name: Columns above, wordmark below
sections.blueprint: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto). Top row, 40px from the edge: four small columns on the 12-column grid (address, navigation, social, hours or contact), each a plain list at 15–16px with its first line in the full ink and the rest in the softer ink. Middle row: empty. Bottom row: the wordmark alone, sized to run from the left margin to the right margin on one line. Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune `font-size` in `vw` to the letter count, so it never wraps; its baseline sits 20px above a single line of legal text at 13px. With `position: sticky; bottom: 0` and a lower `z-index` than the page, the last section slides away to uncover it.
sections.mobile: Columns become two by two at 15px with 32px between rows, at the top. A gap of about 20svh follows. The wordmark spans the full width at the bottom; a name longer than ten letters stacks on two lines, each fitted to the width. Legal line beneath at 12px.

references.name: Spatial
references.idea: Typography behaves like sound in a room: plain black statements swell, stretch and bend through an empty white viewport as you scroll.
references.hero: A white viewport holding only the festival dates: two centred lines in Neue Haas Grotesk Roman at roughly 6.7vw, black, tight leading, sitting at the exact vertical middle and spanning about half the width. Large empty fields above and below; no image, no button, no supporting copy. The header is the only other element: a light uppercase wordmark with tight tracking flush to the top-left corner at a 20px inset, and nine small bold uppercase links in a row across the top right. Mobile is the same poster at 40px with a two-line hamburger.
references.type: One face, Neue Haas Grotesk Display 55 Roman, for everything: statements from 56px up to about 10vw, 13px body, bold 13px uppercase navigation, a timetable at about 16px with tight leading. Statement lines are distorted per glyph, each letter scaled to a different width and height.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e8a25c — Pure black on pure white; the programme section inverts to white on black. The only colour is the amber haze of a single photograph.
references.imagery: Almost none. The images are canvas-rendered text statements warped and magnified until letter fragments become abstract black shapes cropped by the viewport. One warm, hazy venue photograph sits inset at half width beside body copy, square-cornered.
references.layout: Full width with 10 to 20px margins. Opens with one centred statement per screen, then drops into left-aligned two-column copy and, further down, edge-to-edge four-column timetables. The swing between empty poster screens and tightly packed listings is the page's rhythm.

sections.description: A run of full-viewport white screens, each carrying one centred two-line sentence. The text is drawn on canvas and deformed: letters within a word have different widths and heights and baselines wobble. Between screens the type is magnified so far that only the strokes and counters of a few letters cross the frame, cropped on every side, while a small readable version of the next sentence appears inside the wreckage of the previous one.

A calm reset: a three-line centred statement at about 5vw in undistorted type fills the top half. At the bottom, a column of 16px body copy about 650px wide sits flush to the left margin, and an amber-toned photograph starts at the horizontal centre and runs to the right margin with square corners, cropped by the fold.

Black full-bleed section. Day headings are single small lines above a hairline; under each, a four-column table spans the full width: artist flush left, format at one third, room at two thirds, time range right-aligned at the far edge. Rows are about 35px high with a hairline between each, all in the same 30px grotesk with no bold; changeovers are marked by rows in capitals.

steal: Open with a single factual line (the dates) centred on an otherwise empty white screen instead of a branded hero.
Scale each letter of a statement independently in width and height so plain grotesk type looks as if it is resonating.
Set a programme as a full-width four-column hairline table in one size and weight, times right-aligned, on an inverted background.

references.name: CoffeeTech®
references.idea: Present an industrial roaster maker like a design brand: one enormous three-word statement on black, with the machine withheld until the first scroll, where it emerges from the dark.
references.hero: Near-black viewport with nothing but type. A centred three-line headline, one word per line, in Inter Medium at about 15vw with tight tracking; the first line starts a third of the way down and the last runs to within 35px of the bottom edge, its widest word spanning roughly 70% of the width. Cream letters; no subhead, no media, no hero button. Navigation is one quiet row: logo with a terracotta mark at left, four text links centred, then a filled terracotta 'Products' button with a grid icon, an outlined contact button and a language dropdown at right. The top third stays empty.
references.type: Inter throughout at weight 500. Display lines at 216px with -0.07em tracking and leading near 0.95 against 14px body, a jump of about 15 times. Secondary headlines near 10vw, intro paragraph around 26px. Section labels are tiny and wrapped in square brackets.
references.colour: #0d0e13 #e5e2dd #f3ece2 #c8603d #262629 — Blue-black and warm putty-grey sections alternate; cream type on dark, near-black on light. Terracotta appears only on the logo mark and the primary button.
references.imagery: Studio shots of roasters: a black machine barely lit against black after the hero, then white and black machines as cut-outs on pale-grey tiles. One warm founder portrait with a signature overlapping its edge; macro bean photos in small-radius cards.
references.layout: Outer margins of about 70px. A centred type poster on top, then an offset two-column intro, then a product grid pushed into the right two-thirds with its bracketed label alone in the left third. Oversized left-flush headlines open and close the lower page.

sections.description: Warm putty-grey band entered through a hairline. A portrait about 290px wide with 8px corners sits in the left third; a scrawled signature overlaps its bottom-right corner and spills onto the background. A seven-line paragraph at about 26px, medium weight, roughly 510px wide, begins at the horizontal midpoint, followed by a small underlined text link. No heading; the right quarter and the gap between the two elements stay empty.

A headline at roughly 10vw is flush to the left edge and clipped by the right, like a slow marquee. Below, a tiny bracketed label sits alone in the left third; the right two-thirds hold a two-column grid of pale-grey tiles about 400px wide with a small radius, each with a centred machine cut-out, the model name beneath and a tiny outlined pill for its category. The grid closes with a 64px underlined 'see all' text link with an arrow.

Back to blue-black. A cream contact headline at about 10vw sits hard against the left edge, far larger than anything near it. Underneath, the terracotta logo mark is enlarged to about 140px at left; four narrow link columns in small grey text run from 28% to 85% of the width; a pill-shaped back-to-top button sits at far right, with a thin legal row at the bottom.

steal: Let a three-word headline at about 15vw be the entire first viewport and withhold the product until the first scroll.
Photograph a dark product on a background matching the page colour so it appears to emerge from the page rather than sit in a box.
Overlap a handwritten signature onto the corner of a portrait so an about block feels signed rather than laid out.

references.name: Pensatori Irrazionali
references.idea: The client roster becomes the hero object, a 3D sheaf of logo-printed fabric ribbons, and classical Italian ornament (copperplate script, engravings, tricolour) is collided with plain Helvetica.
references.archetype: other: offset 3d object with bottom-left statement
references.hero: Flat pale-grey field (#f5f5f5). A 3D-rendered bundle of woven fabric ribbons, each a different saturated colour and printed with a client logo, streams diagonally from beyond the top-right corner down to about centre-left, covering roughly the right two-thirds and bleeding off the top and right edges. Top-left: a small engraved lion crest with serif wordmark and a green-white-red bar. Top-right: two dark square icon buttons with chamfered corners. Bottom-left, in the lowest fifth: a tiny '+ (Atelier)' label above a three-line grey intro paragraph at about 36px, half the viewport wide. No headline and no call to action; the left third is empty.
references.type: Helvetica Now at regular weight does nearly everything, tracking -0.025em, sentence case, from 14px body to 60px menu links. Section titles pair it with huge hairline copperplate script words, and the footer wordmark is a heavy high-contrast serif at about 18vw.
references.colour: #f5f5f5 #434343 #292828 #e9e9e9 #e3342a #2bd92b — One pale grey ground throughout with charcoal rather than black text. Saturated colour is confined to the ribbon render and project images, plus a green and red flag underline and one neon-green dot.
references.imagery: Hero 3D render of logo-printed textile ribbons; black engraved illustrations (angel, Pegasus, lion) cut out and placed inside headings; dark-grey map silhouettes; square-cornered project stills in a horizontal row.
references.layout: Narrow 48px side margins with content hung on a loose two-column split at 50%. Sections alternate between oversized title bands that bleed off both edges and small hairline-ruled tabular lists, with generous blank grey between blocks.

sections.description: A title band runs edge to edge as one line: a hairline copperplate script word about 250px tall cropped by the left edge, a tiny superscript '(01)', a black engraving of an angel dropped in like an inline glyph, then a grotesk phrase at 90px running off the right edge. Beneath, two columns of client rows: name at about 40px, a tiny grey category label, the client's logo mark, a small arrow, each row closed by a hairline.

A grid of five columns by two rows of equal cells with faint 1px borders, each holding one small monochrome client logo, centred. Directly below, a wide empty band works as a map: a dark-grey country silhouette crops in at each side edge, with a two-line place name at 32px bottom-left and another bottom-right, each with tiny coordinates in parentheses underneath.

The same script-plus-engraving title band, now with a Pegasus and '(02)'. Below, a two-column table headed by tiny 'Number' and 'Service' labels over a hairline: the left column shows a giant hairline script numeral about 200px tall; the right holds a small '+ (Branding)' label, a service name with a neon-green dot, and ruled rows pairing a term at left with a grey descriptor right-aligned.

The first word of the name in a heavy high-contrast serif spans the full width and crops at the right edge (about 18vw), with a green underline under its left half and red under its right. Behind and below, the second word in giant pale-grey gradient script overlaps the serif letters. Under that, small columns: menu links at 18px, contact details at 11px, legal links at right.

steal: Turn the client-logo list into one physical object (logos printed on a rendered bundle of ribbons) so proof becomes the hero image instead of a logo strip.
Build section titles as one edge-to-edge line mixing a hairline script word, an inline engraved illustration and a plain grotesk phrase at similar height.
Keep the page on one pale grey with charcoal text and let colour enter only through imagery and a single flag-coloured underline on the footer wordmark.
